A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DLoRAL research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, inference measurements, a ten-volunteer user study, and training-strategy ablations in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds component-removal, separately trained LoRA-branch, and temporal-window ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same CFR module, two LoRA branches, losses, alternating training, and one-step inference. Figure 2 renames Enhancement-LoRA to Detail-LoRA consistently with the existing text; the added ablations do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training still uses REDS/Pexels and LSDIR, with evaluation on UDM10, SPMCS, RealVSR, and VideoLQ. VideoLQ4 already appeared in v1 Appendix A.2. The new ablations introduce no additional dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: v3 adds internal comparison variants: models without CFR, C-LoRA, or D-LoRA in Table 3, and separately trained branch-only models in Table A1. The seven external benchmark baselines and the efficiency and user-study comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New ablation designs include component removals with other settings held fixed, branch-only variants trained from scratch, and CFR windows of 0, 1, 3, and 5. The retained training-order comparison drops BRISQUE and DOVER from its reported metric set. The newly disclosed benchmark cropping does not establish a changed or rerun experiment.

E4.justification: v1 investigates optimization strategies and training-stage order. v3 retains these analyses and substantially expands diagnostic coverage to individual component necessity (Table 3), separately trained LoRA-branch roles (Table A1), and temporal-window sensitivity (Table A3), directly testing previously unisolated design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for these comparisons. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting; the existing training curves do not represent repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Changes are confined to ablation results. New entries include MUSIQ 54.0769 without D-LoRA versus 66.6174 for the full model, and 62.1562 with CFR window 5. The training-order table loses BRISQUE and DOVER entries but retains its other values. Main benchmark scores, efficiency measurements, and user-study votes are unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulation, CFR equations, loss definitions, transition interpolation, and warping-error definition are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about decoupled LoRA learning, degradation-robust temporal priors, restoration quality, and one-step efficiency. The additional experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an interpretation of temporal-window sensitivity: larger windows can reduce warping error while sacrificing perceptual quality, motivating the retained window choice. It also expands the rationale for LSDIR pseudo-videos by contrasting their visual quality with video datasets. The existing VAE limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly discloses that real-world benchmark videos were centrally cropped to 128 × 128. Appendix A.2 specifies from-scratch training for the branch-only comparison. VideoLQ4 clip identities were already supplied in v1; hardware, optimizer, and code/model access information remain unchanged. New Table A1 does not clearly distinguish VideoLQ from its four-clip subset.

R1.justification: The 54 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained, including positioning relative to PiSA-SR and existing diffusion-based VSR methods. No new research relationship or novelty claim is introduced.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to expanded dataset justification, a new main-text ablation paragraph, additional Appendix A.2 subsections, revised appendix contents, and author/venue information. The overall organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 3, A1, and A3, narrows the former Table A1 after renumbering it A2, and adjusts Figure 2 terminology and spacing. Existing figures and user-study displays are retained, with modest layout shifts around the additions.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's training-strategy ablations, v3 adds direct component and window tests that better substantiate design choices, while disclosing evaluation cropping. These focused gains outweigh losing two metrics from the training-order comparison. Unchanged main results, absent uncertainty estimates, and unclear subset labeling in Table A1 limit the overall improvement.
